scenes.heading: Spotting and handling chargebacks and payment fraud

sents.d: Spotting and handling chargebacks and payment fraud
Most chargebacks are avoidable friction, not fraud — but the ones that are fraud have real warning signs.

A rushed order with mismatched billing/shipping addresses, an unusually large first-time order, or a buyer requesting expedited shipping to a freight forwarder are common fraud warning signs worth a manual review before fulfilling, especially for higher-ticket items.

For legitimate disputes, responding quickly with your evidence (tracking, delivery confirmation, customer communication) to the payment processor's chargeback process matters — many merchants lose winnable disputes simply by not responding in time.

A chargeback rate that creeps too high can put your payment processing account at risk, so tracking your rate over time and tightening fraud screening if it climbs is worth doing before it becomes a bigger problem.

take: Review risky orders and answer chargebacks quickly with evidence.
